Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testNoHeaderMap()` verifies that when a parser is created from CSV content with no headers specified (`CSVFormat.DEFAULT` without headers or skipHeaderRecord), the `getHeaderMap()` method returns null. This test fails because `getHeaderMap()` throws a NullPointerException (NPE).

Looking at the `CSVParser.getHeaderMap()` method (lines 287-289), we see it returns a new `LinkedHashMap` constructed from the `headerMap` field. However, if `headerMap` is null, this will throw an NPE because `LinkedHashMap` cannot be constructed from a null argument.

The `headerMap` field is initialized during construction by the method `initializeHeader()` (lines 324-352). This method looks at the format's header setting. If `format.getHeader()` is null (meaning no header is set), `hdrMap` remains null and is returned as null. Hence, `headerMap` can be null for no-header CSV formats.

In this case, the `CSVFormat.DEFAULT` implies no headers, so `initializeHeader()` returns null, and `headerMap` is set to null. Later, calling `getHeaderMap()` tries to return a new LinkedHashMap from a null map, causing the NPE.

The test expects `getHeaderMap()` to return null if no headers exist. The bug is that `getHeaderMap()` does not check for null before creating the new map, causing the crash.

Therefore, the root cause is the missing null check in `getHeaderMap()`, causing it to throw an NPE when no headers are set, instead of returning null as expected by the test `testNoHeaderMap()`.

No relevant recent bug reports were found to add additional context. The issue is a straightforward null dereference caused by returning a copy of a possibly null map without checking.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
